text:
Alex C: Heads up — canary for SDK 2.1.0 rolled out ~30m ago and we're seeing paging failures on streaming endpoints. customers report hangs / EOFs when following next_page tokens.

incident-bot: Severity: high — multiple customers affected. Trigger: automated paging errors > 5% of requests in canary.

Alex C: Repro on staging with client 2.1.0 — server returns 200 but stream closes after first page. Error in logs: `paging: invalid continuation token` repeated.

QA Eng: I can repro with the example from support ticket #4571. Minimal repro: request page 1, then pass token to stream-next -> immediate EOF.

Maria P: tagging SRE Oncall — can you take lead for mitigation? @SRE Oncall

SRE Oncall: taking it. Thanks. Quick status: canary was 5% of traffic in us-west. Error rate on canary hosts = 18% for paging endpoints, global user impact ~2-3% but concentrated on high-traffic customers.

Jen L: any recent infra changes? deploy-bot, what changed in deployment?

Deploy Bot: Canary deployment for sdk-service v2.1.0 completed at 1839121200. No infra config changes recorded.

Alex C: root cause hypothesis — we changed token encoding in SDK 2.1 to support compressed tokens; server expects legacy format. Compat check missed because non-streaming pages still work. Streaming flow validates token shape differently.

SRE Oncall: ok immediate mitigation options: 1) kill canary FF so traffic doesn't route to 2.1.0, 2) rollback canary hosts to 2.0.5, 3) quick server-side shim to accept new token shape. Which is fastest?

Maria P: FF toggle is fastest for immediately stopping new canary traffic. I can flip it. Jen, prepare rollback if FF toggle doesn't stabilize.

Jen L: I'll prepare rollback plan and coordinate with infra. Rollback to 2.0.5 on canary pool; will take ~8-12m once triggered.

Maria P: flipping feature flag now in Console -> Routing -> CanaryPools -> sdk-2.1.0 -> disable.

Maria P: :white_check_mark: FF kill-switch toggled at 1839122250. Monitoring...

incident-bot: Canary traffic to sdk-service v2.1.0 reduced from 5% to 0% at 1839122260. Error rate dropped to baseline on main pool.

SRE Oncall: good — immediate customer impact should stop. But we still need rollback for any hosts that already pulled 2.1.0 binary. Jen, proceed with rollback on canary pool to be safe.

Jen L: rolling back canary hosts. Command: ```kubectl set image deploy/sdk-service sdk-service=redwood/sdk-service:2.0.5-canary -n prod-canary``` Starting now. Will post when done.

QA Eng: from and after FF kill, I still see a few in-flight failures for requests that already hit canary sessions. Those are expected to clear out.

support-bot: open ticket update drafted to affected customers — advising we killed canary and are rolling back, ETA for full mitigation 20-30m. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/t/4571

Jen L: rollback complete on canary at 1839122800. Health checks green.

SRE Oncall: monitoring metrics — paged stream errors dropped to baseline within 3 minutes of rollback. No new customers reporting regressions.

Alex C: root cause triage notes: SDK 2.1 changed continuation token format (base64 urlsafe with checksum) but server-side parser used strict legacy decode path. Fuzz tests should have caught this but our integration test mocked non-streaming path only.

Maria P: action items: 1) urgent - add server-side compatibility shim to accept both token formats (owner: Alex C, 24h). 2) expand regression tests to include streaming paging with full token roundtrip across SDK+server (owner: QA Eng, 48h). 3) update release checklist to include token-compat e2e (owner: Maria P). 4) Cherry-pick patch to release branch if needed (owner: Alex C).

Alex C: I will open PR for shim and post link. Also will prepare patch to SDK to fallback to legacy encoding when server rejects.

SRE Oncall: post-incident customer impact assessment: approx 6 customers experienced degraded paging during the window; two enterprise customers filed high-severity tickets but no data loss. Cost/latency impact limited. Recommend proactive outreach to the two enterprise customers.

Support-bot: scheduled customer outreach messages drafted. Pending review from CS.

Maria P: handoff — SRE Oncall handing back to Maria P for follow-up ownership at 1839123500. Any outstanding monitoring alarms?

SRE Oncall: no active alarms. We'll keep an eye for 1h and then close.

Jen L: logging playbook snippets added to runbook: how to identify invalid token errors and rollback steps.

Alex C: PRs: shim PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-service/pull/1123 (WIP). SDK fallback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/789 (WIP).

Maria P: thanks everyone. Postmortem owner: Maria P. Draft due in 48h. Include timeline, impact, root cause, and action items.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) at 1839124070. Severity: high -> mitigated.

Alex C: notes for the postmortem: include test matrix, why canary didn't catch it, and improve canary traffic isolation for streaming-sensitive endpoints.

Support-bot: will follow up with CS drafts and send updates to affected customers once PM approves.

Maria P: closing thread for now. If anyone sees regression ping asap. :thumbsup:
